items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: If you listen carefully, in some of the early singers like Sister Rosetta Tharpe, Rosetta Tharpe, anything that she sang could have been transposed and made into a spiritual in church.

ctx.x: Do you think your experience playing in church, playing in the choirs— what influence did those experiences have on shaping you as an artist.

Well, I think that all of those—Well, I think playing religious music, particularly spirituals had a great impact on shaping my perspective on what jazz is about. If you listen carefully, in some of the early singers like Sister Rosetta Tharpe, Rosetta Tharpe, anything that she sang could have been transposed and made into a spiritual in church. When she sang, in a nightclub setting, it became blues. But, it’s the same style. A lot of the music, when you move it from one venue to another, it takes on a different…
Could you identify some specifics that you think crossover? Must we leave it as a generalization?
